title: The access test
intro: Four questions to ask before any business agent receives production access.
steps: Inventory
Name every account, folder, tool and permission the role can reach.
Authority
Separate instructions from the owner from untrusted web and email content.
Approval
Identify writes, external messages and spending that require a person.
Evidence
Request a successful, rejected and failed example before expansion.
practice: Choose one real action, such as sending a reply. Ask the provider to show the allowed scope, a denied attempt and the audit record.

insight.title: An email is not permission.
insight.left: An incoming message asks for a full customer export.
insight.right: Only agreed tasks can reach customer data. Export is denied.
insight.lesson: Content an agent reads must not rewrite its access rules.
insight.definition: The accounts, files and actions software is allowed to use.

title: The four boundaries of an accountable agent
intro: Read the sequence as a security requirement for every meaningful tool action, not a claim that a particular agent is deployed.
steps: Identity
Identify the agent, requesting person and accountable business owner.
Permission
Limit the tools, data, destination and lifetime to this specific job.
Enforcement
Make the execution layer independently reject prohibited actions.
Evidence
Verify the external result and retain a minimal, useful audit record.
practice: Choose a sensitive action. Ask the provider to demonstrate the approved path, a forbidden path and a partial failure using only synthetic data.

insight.title: The model can propose. The system must decide.
insight.left: The assistant says it will never send unapproved information.
insight.right: The execution service blocks an unauthorised send regardless of the model's text.
insight.lesson: Security is the difference between a polite answer and an action the system cannot perform.
insight.definition: Giving software only the minimum rights required to complete an agreed task.

title: The memory lifecycle
intro: Context becomes useful when facts have ownership, review and expiry.
steps: Collect
Use a named, approved business source rather than an unsupported recollection.
Attribute
Record who owns the information and when it was last checked.
Retrieve
Return only knowledge the role is permitted to access.
Correct
Amend, archive or delete stale knowledge with a documented process.
practice: Select one important company rule. Trace its source, owner, access permissions and correction path before putting it into an agent.

insight.title: Same question. Different answers.
insight.left: An old PDF contains an outdated refund rule.
insight.right: A dated, approved policy names who can update it.
insight.lesson: When sources disagree, check the owner and current policy.
insight.definition: Information a business has approved for specific people or software to use.

title: The agent's working loop
intro: The value is not a clever reply. It is a verifiable result from permitted action.
steps: Request
Receive a defined job with the necessary context.
Choose
Select a permitted tool and a next step.
Act
Use the scoped browser, file or connector access.
Verify
Inspect the real output and escalate an uncertain result.
practice: Describe one job in three lines: what starts it, what tools it may use and what evidence proves completion.

insight.title: A reply is not a finished task.
insight.right: Confirm the intended record or draft is saved in the right place.
insight.lesson: Judge completion from the actual business system, not a chat message.
insight.definition: An application or function software can use to perform an action.

title: When the clean path breaks
intro: A recovery diagram. A failed tool call must not be treated as proof that no action occurred.
steps: Interrupt
A login fails, a source disappears or a tool call times out.
Inspect
Read the last known external state, not just the agent transcript.
Decide
Retry safely only if duplicate changes can be ruled out.
Recover
Escalate, record the gap and resume from a verified checkpoint.
practice: Rehearse a timeout just after a simulated write. Check that the workflow does not send or update twice.

insight.title: A timeout is not a cancellation.
insight.left: The connection stops before a confirmation arrives.
insight.right: The customer record could already have changed.
insight.lesson: Inspect the external record before another attempt.
insight.definition: When software stops waiting for a response; the requested action may still have happened.

title: Answering versus operating
intro: A service role is defined by the tools, accountability and boundary around it.
steps: Conversation
The system can explain or draft information.
Assigned role
A recurring task receives an owner and acceptance criteria.
Tool access
Specific accounts and permitted actions are configured.
Service review
Output, failures and human support are measured separately.
practice: Ask a vendor to name one agreed recurring job, its success criteria, its exceptions and the support person responsible for it.

insight.title: Advice and responsibility are different.
insight.left: A helpful answer is given to a person.
insight.right: A defined task produces a checked result with a named owner.
insight.lesson: The difference is the agreed work and oversight, not a magical model.
insight.definition: A person reviews the work and remains responsible for important decisions.

title: Four layers of practical AI
intro: A vocabulary that moves from prediction to a bounded business system.
steps: Model
Produces or transforms content from provided context.
Workflow
Organises steps, triggers and checking around that model.
Agent
Can choose tool calls within the work process.
Governance
Restricts access, confirms outputs and names a responsible person.
practice: Take a familiar task. Identify which parts genuinely require a model and which would be more reliable as ordinary rules.

insight.title: Not every step needs AI.
insight.left: Can read information and draft a reply.
insight.right: Checks the information, follows rules and asks for approval.
insight.lesson: Use ordinary rules where they are more predictable than AI.
insight.definition: A repeatable sequence of steps that turns an input into an expected result.

title: What a fair comparison includes
intro: A decision map for comparing service cost against the work actually performed.
steps: Baseline
Count today's task frequency, effort and error correction.
Scope
Specify one workflow, permissions, volume and exclusions.
Full cost
Add human approval, support, tools and exception handling.
Measure
Review accepted outputs before claiming time or cash savings.
practice: Use your own last month of work to record volume and review time. Compare it against the written scope, not an advertised percentage.

insight.title: A price is not the full cost.
insight.left: The monthly amount on the proposal.
insight.right: The same work, plus tools, review, support and failures.
insight.lesson: Compare accepted work with the full cost of delivering it.
insight.definition: Work checked against the standard agreed before it started.

title: The real cost stack
intro: Model usage is just one operating component; responsibilities matter more than headline rates.
steps: Design
Map the task and prepare suitable company data.
Connect
Configure business tools and authorised accounts.
Operate
Budget for usage, hosting, review and monitoring.
Maintain
Allow for changes, incidents and recovery work.
practice: Request a quote that separates setup, tools, usage, maintenance and support. Ask who pays each line when activity doubles.

insight.title: Cheap model calls can be expensive jobs.
insight.left: The charge for generating or analysing content.
insight.right: Setup, tools, hosting, checking, maintenance and recovery.
insight.lesson: Ask who pays for the work around the model.
insight.definition: Software trained to process information and generate or classify content.

title: A practical first-job filter
intro: Good starting tasks are frequent, bounded and easy for a named owner to inspect.
steps: Find
Pick a recurring task with a recognizable input.
Limit
Exclude sensitive decisions and out-of-scope access.
Trial
Check representative outputs and inconvenient edge cases.
Review
Keep, revise or stop based on evidence and effort.
practice: Choose just one inbox, report or follow-up job. Set a review date and one measurable acceptance test.

insight.title: Start smaller than the sales pitch.
insight.right: Prepare one repeat reply for a person to check.
insight.lesson: A small, reviewable job makes problems easier to find and fix.
insight.definition: A job with a clear beginning, end and limits.

title: The complete call journey
intro: Assess the journey end to end, rather than a per-minute headline.
steps: Answer
Identify what the caller needs and disclose the system appropriately.
Understand
Confirm names, consent and unclear requests.
Handoff
Route complex, urgent or sensitive calls to a person.
Verify
Check the actual booking or CRM entry after the call.
practice: Try a noisy call, an interrupted caller and a request beyond the script. Verify the hand-off and the written record.

insight.title: Answering is not resolving.
insight.left: An automated voice picks up the call.
insight.right: Identify the request, confirm details, hand off and check the booking.
insight.lesson: Price the completed call journey, not only voice processing.
insight.definition: When software sends the work to a person with enough context to continue.

title: Automation changes a task bundle
intro: A historical analogy is not a forecast of employment or customer demand.
steps: List
Separate administration from judgement and relationships.
Automate
Select bounded tasks with clear acceptance criteria.
Reallocate
Decide what people will do with the released time.
Observe
Measure service quality and unexpected consequences.
practice: Ask the people who perform the task what exceptions a process document misses, then include those cases in the trial.

insight.title: One task is not a whole job.
insight.left: A machine handles many cash withdrawals.
insight.right: Service, advice, exceptions and customer relationships.
insight.lesson: Do not turn an analogy into a prediction about staffing.
insight.definition: Using technology to carry out specified tasks with less manual effort.

title: Capability is not permission
intro: Future model intelligence does not replace real-world security engineering.
steps: Identify
Name the deployed model, tools, data and environment.
Constrain
Apply least privilege and approval limits.
Challenge
Test bad instructions, missing context and forbidden actions.
Revalidate
Repeat the evaluation after model or tool changes.
practice: Write a prohibited-action test and confirm the real application refuses the action, rather than merely saying that it would refuse.

insight.title: More capable does not mean unrestricted.
insight.left: A system handles a difficult reasoning question.
insight.right: The connected application refuses an unapproved data export.
insight.lesson: Test the actual boundary where work happens.
insight.definition: A rule enforced by the software or service that limits what another system can do.
